The Riksdag has implemented restrictions on immigration that had been in development over several months. The policy change is seen as a victory for the Swedish Democrats, the far-right party and leading voice of opposition to Sweden's open immigration policy. Public disapproval of immigration had been growing ever since the grenade attacks on Malmo back in July of 2015. Recent events such as ISIS calling on sleeper cells to attack and the exodus of 300,000 swedes to Norway are evidence of a turning point in swedish mentality and sense of security. In recent polls 62% of Swedish citizens supported amending immigration policies to limit the flow of immigrants, up from 43% before the Norwegian exodus.

Politicians in the ruling Social Democrats party have ceded their immigration stance in favor of supporting integration of current immigrant populations and stress these restrictions are only temporary.

Prior to this change Sweden took in more refugees per capita than any country in Europe. Immigration services are predicting that over 100,000 asylum requests to Sweden will be made this year. As a small nation, Sweden cannot continue to open the doors to large numbers of asylum seekers like it's larger partners in Europe. The Riksdag has decided on a 15,000 cap on accepting asylum requests per year.

The financial burden was among the main arguments that pushed legislation forward. The Swedish government takes the responsibility of supporting refugees financially. The situation does not improve later on as immigrant populations suffer disproportionately from unemployment which stands at 7% and it was argued that Sweden does not have the jobs that migrants so desperately seek. Stopping flows of migrants now will ease a burdened welfare system and allow Sweden to focus on the people already here. The Riksdag managed to compromise a 50% cut in immigration requests, a much lower figure than the 90% the Sweden Democrats had originally campaigned for.

Urban Ahlin, Speaker of the Riksdag, wanted to state to Sweden's neighbors that "the rights of the European Citizen to live and work in another EU member state shall not be infringed, and immigration of EU citizens is exempt from the restrictions... we will also uphold agreements with our fellow nordic countries that allow our citizens the right to live in any nordic country they choose."

Bravo Sweden.

What I'd do is develop the plot further in subzones and provide players an incentive to access old world content via a planned Adventure Mode:

Kalimdor:

  • The Lost Isles are moved to a non-instanced part of Kalimdor, off the Eastern coast and on the isle, the new Bilgewater Cartel capital city is established.
  • A major Darkspear Troll city is established in Durotar, the Echo Isles become their own zone.
  • The Cenarion Circle build a dam in Thousand Needles and drain the zone of its water. The entire zone becomes greener as a result and life begins to repopulate it including the Grimtotem Clan and the Shimmering Flats becomes a racetrack once again. The result is a redesigned 40 - 45 zone and a new Level 48 (110 Heroic) instance focused around the Grimtotem Clan.
  • Garrosh Hellscream is only replaced with Vol'jin once the player hits level 90 in Pandaria - in an attempt to fix the continuity of the game.
  • As the lava-filled chasm separating the Northern and Southern Barrens thaws, a bridge is built to connect the two zones.

Eastern Kingdoms:

  • Gilneas and Gnomeregan are retaken by the Alliance and become Alliance capital cities in their own right.
  • A bridge is built to connect the Badlands with Loch Modan.
  • The Western Plaguelands is now known as Northern Lordaeron and the Eastern Plaguelands is simply known as the Plaguelands. The battle between the Alliance and Forsaken continues.
  • Reinforcements have been removed from Alterac Valley, and the area has become an instanced 110 PvP zone with epic 40v40 battles reminiscent of Vanilla WoW. As a result, Alterac Valley has been phased out as a battleground and reputation gains made previously have now been reset. Those who did a rep grind previously can earn a Feat of Strength.
  • A new level 110 dungeon (Deadwind Crypt) is available, and can be accessed from the underground crypt near Karazhan in Deadwind Pass.

Northrend:

  • Azjol'Nerub is now accessible as a subterranean endgame zone beneath Dragonblight.
  • A new 110 raid (Nerubian Palace) is available, continuing the post-Wrath plot of Northrend where a new Nerubian leader has taken command of the remnants of the Nerubian Empire and now threatens the safety of those in Northrend.

Draenor:

  • A new 110 raid (Battle for Shattrath) is available. Accompany Grommash, Y'rel and Durotan in liberating the Draenei capital of Shattrath and restoring peace to Draenor once and for all.
  • The Alliance and Horde capitals have been relocated to Temple of Karabor and Bladespire Citadel respectively.
